citations.narrative:
The perimeter fence contained multiple deficiencies that reduced its ability to restrict access to the marine mammal facility
by unauthorized persons or animals. The woven wooden perimeter fence along the north side of the property had rotted,
detached boards that no longer formed a continuous barrier. There was a section with a missing lower slat that created a
gap approximately 8 inches high and 8 feet wide. Areas of washout were observed in both the northern wooden and
southern chain-link sections of perimeter fence, creating gaps under the fence up to 9 inches high and 2 feet wide. A
vertical support pole on the chain-link perimeter fence boarding the southern side of the property was rusted, broken and
detached at the base. Sections of floating dock were observed stacked approximately 2.5 feet high and stored against the
6-foot chain-link fence. Sheets of corrugated metal stacked approximately 2 feet high and 8 feet wide were also seen
stored against chain-link perimeter fence.
Stored materials against the perimeter fence reduce the effective height of the barrier. Gaps and openings may allow
unauthorized persons and animals to enter and exit the area and gain access to the animals within.
The perimeter fence must be constructed so that it protects marine mammals by restricting animals and unauthorized
persons from going through it or under it and having contact with the marine mammals, and so that it can function as a
secondary containment system for the animals in the facility when appropriate. To be corrected by August 26, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
